_note: Every number the model uses lives here. 'source' says where it comes from. Charts, cited sources and open questions: docs/economics/README.md

house.source: DigitalHeat case brief (reference house). hot_water_shape=flat is OUR assumption; overridden when the case CSV is passed with --profile.

server.source: Case brief. idle_power_kw=0 is OUR simplification: a paused server is assumed to draw nothing.

prices.source: electricity: PLACEHOLDER = ElCom 2026 Swiss H4 median (27.7 Rp). REPLACE with IWB Basel H4 total from strompreis.elcom.admin.ch. COP: case brief. compute price: OUR assumption, shown only against the break-even.

interactive.label: Interactive sessions (local AI chat, game streaming)
interactive.source: OUR scenario: one evening session block of 4 h per house and day.

batch.label: Batch with deadline (transcription)
batch.source: Whisper large-v3 speech to text, the MLPerf Inference speech benchmark since v5.1. Interruptible per recording. Deadline 24 h: OpenAI Batch API completion window. Size: 24.7 GPU-s per audio hour (Open ASR Leaderboard RTFx 145.51 on A100), 2.75 Wh for the GPU at its 400 W TDP, host not counted, about 360 audio hours per 1 kW server-hour. 8 server-hours at 06:00 is OUR scenario. Sources: docs/job-types.md

opportunistic.label: Opportunistic backlog (embeddings)
opportunistic.source: ASSUMES AN UNLIMITED BACKLOG of deadline-free work (fleet-level queue). This is the single most optimistic assumption in the model. Job size measured on our machine: 0.113 Wh and 34.2 CPU-s per 200,000 items, about 8,840 jobs per 1 kW server-hour (docs/measurements.md).

fleet.source: OUR synthetic scenario for make fleet (heatsched/fleet_scenario.py): every house is made up, drawn evenly from these ranges with this seed, on the real Basel 2025 weather. space_heating_scale multiplies the reference house's space heating. Unlike the one-house model, the backlog is finite and due within backlog_deadline_h, so work the houses cannot take shows up as moved to a data centre.

hardware._note: Per 1 kW server unless a name says per house. CHF without VAT. Dollar and pound prices converted at the ECB reference rates of 20 Nov 2026 (1 USD = 0.8392 CHF, 1 GBP = 1.1015 CHF). Each source is below; anything marked OUR GUESS has none yet. Charts and links: docs/economics/README.md

source.server_chf: low and high: the range USD 3,000 to 8,000 for a refurbished single-GPU inference host (PCSP, 'How much does a server cost in 2026?', 21 Aug 2026). mid: a new single-GPU AI workstation with an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (up to 600 W), from USD 5,999 (VRLA Tech, 30 Jun 2026). That each draws about 1 kW in use is OUR GUESS.
source.cooling_kit_chf: A custom water loop for CPU and GPU costs GBP 450 to 700 (Watercooling UK, 29 Jul 2026); mid is the midpoint. That a plate heat exchanger to the tank costs about what the loop's radiator does is OUR GUESS.
source.fitter_chf_per_hour: Heating and plumbing rates without VAT, 2025: B-Monteur 103, A-Monteur 120, Chefmonteur 148 CHF an hour (WBAG, Regietarif 2025).
source.electrician_chf_per_hour: Elektroinstallateur EFZ, 151 CHF an hour without VAT (EIT.nordwest, Basel, recommended rates 2026).
source.hours_per_house: Fitter and electrician hours to fit six servers to the tank: OUR GUESS.
source.service: Service fitter with van 125 CHF an hour, call-out 65 CHF (WBAG, Regietarif 2025). Visits and hours a year: OUR GUESS.
source.lifetime_years: 6: the large cloud providers' server life by 2023 (SiliconANGLE, 22 Nov 2025). 5: Amazon, for part of its servers from 1 Jan 2025 (Amazon 10-K 2025). 4: Amazon from 2020 (SiliconANGLE).
source.discount_rate: 3.28%: WACC for Swiss power grids, tariff year 2027 (UVEK, 2 Mar 2026). 3.75%: WACC for PV investment contributions 2026 (pv magazine, 2 Mar 2026). 6%: OUR GUESS for a young, riskier business.

solar._note: Roof PV and a home battery that power the servers (issue #27). Used by economics.py for charts 8 to 10; the base results above run without them. CHF without VAT. Each source is below; anything marked OUR GUESS has none yet. Charts and links: docs/economics/README.md

source.roof_kwp: 10 kWp on a 30° south roof: OUR GUESS for a Basel single-family roof, about 50 m². Swissolar: about 25 m² of PV covers a 4-person household's 4,000 kWh (Faktenblatt PV Schweiz, Jul 2025).
source.yield_model: Sun position (Spencer 1971), direct and diffuse split (Erbs, Klein and Duffie 1982), tilted roof with the isotropic sky (Liu and Jordan 1963), on the Open-Meteo hourly radiation already in the repo. Gives 1,167 kWh per kWp in 2025; PVGIS 5.3 gives 1,160 for Basel 2005-2023 at 30° south.
source.performance_ratio: 0.79: PVGIS 5.3 total loss for Basel, 30° south, 14% system loss (21.05% in all, incl. heat and angle), JRC, checked 21 Nov 2026.
source.pv_chf_per_kwp: Rooftop systems 10-30 kW in 2025, without VAT: lower quartile 1,659, median 1,911, upper quartile 2,237 CHF per kW (EnergieSchweiz, Photovoltaikmarkt: Preisbeobachtungsstudie 2025, Planair, 3 Aug 2026, Tabelle 4).
source.battery_chf: mid: 432 CHF per kWh + 2,122 CHF, the 2025 regression without VAT (same study, Abbildung 27). low and high: 6,000 to 10,000 CHF for 10-15 kWh in a single-family house (Swissolar, Faktenblatt PV Schweiz, Jul 2025).
source.subsidy_chf_per_kwp: Federal one-off payment (KLEIV) for attached systems under 30 kWp: 360 CHF per kWp (CKW, as of Sep 2025). Set each year by the federal government.
source.feed_in_chf_per_kwh: IWB pays 14 Rp per kWh fed in for systems up to 100 kW, for 12 years (IWB, PV-Rückliefertarif; confirmed for 2026 in IWB's release of 26 Aug 2025). Whether VAT is included is not stated.
source.iwb_2027_chf_per_kwh: IWB Basel 2027 H4 total, 33.42 Rp per kWh without VAT (ElCom, strompreis.elcom.admin.ch, checked 21 Nov 2026). Used as a sensitivity case.
source.lifetimes: PV: 33 years is the mean life of a Swiss PV system (Swissolar, Faktenblatt Jul 2025); 30 and 25 years for the mid and high case, and all battery lives, are OUR GUESS.
source.pv_upkeep_share_per_year: 1% (low, mid) and 1.5% (high) of the PV price a year: OUR GUESS.
source.discount_rate: 3.75%: WACC for PV investment contributions 2026 (pv magazine, 2 Mar 2026).
